title: The maximum Laplacian ratio of a tree: a complete answer to a question of Brualdi and Goldwasser, kernel-checked in Lean
description:
Lean 4 formalization, certificate generators, verification programs and a preprint answering a question of Brualdi and Goldwasser (1984).

Result. For every n ≥ 4, the tree on n vertices maximizing the Laplacian ratio per L(T) / ∏ deg(v) is an explicit spider of cherry arms, and the maximum grows exactly like ((621/64)^(1/11))^n. The maximizer is unique up to isomorphism for every n ≥ 4 except n = 21, where exactly T(3,3,3) and S(21,10) are maximal.

Verification. Kernel-checked in Lean 4 with Mathlib, using only the standard axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). The statement of the maximum and a maximizer is re-checked by a second, independently implemented kernel (nanoda, via the Lean FRO's Comparator), on the current proof terms. Uniqueness (formalization/BGUnique) is checked by Lean's kernel, and Comparator confirms that its statement matches the challenge. For the weighted family pi_lambda, the uniform theorem, with its equality clauses, is formalized in formalization/cherry. The directory computations/ holds the programs behind the computer-verified steps of the accompanying work, each with a README and its expected output, with second implementations and negative controls where available.

Status. Not yet refereed. The proofs and programs were produced with AI assistance; see the README.
